findings.title: Setting documented $HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND env var to any built-in backend name crashes `import hypertools` (UnboundLocalError masking ValueError)
findings.description: hypertools/plot/backend.py:550-556 (_init_backend): when $HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND matches a backend in the built-in candidate list (case-insensitive), the reorder branch calls `backends.index(HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND)` -- but HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND is the module global, still None during init (the local is `env_backend`) -- raising ValueError. The `finally:` block at line 691 then references `working_backend`, never assigned, so the user sees a baffling UnboundLocalError and `import hypertools` fails entirely. Two further latent bugs in the same branch: (a) even with env_backend, `backends.index(env_backend)` would fail on case-mismatch ('tkagg' vs 'TkAgg') since the membership check lowercases but the index call does not; (b) the rebuilt tuple `(backends[: idx], *backends[idx+1:])` nests a TUPLE as element 0, which would later crash `mpl.use()`. The env var is documented in hypertools/plot/plot.py's mpl_backend docstring: 'Set the `$HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND` environment variable ... to override the backend used by auto'. Confirmed for TkAgg, tkagg, MacOSX, QtAgg; not-in-list values (WebAgg, plotly, nonsense) do NOT crash (WebAgg honored; others warn and fall back).

findings.title: A single failed backend switch permanently corrupts backend-management state (IN_SET_CONTEXT stuck True; HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND left at the bad value; BACKEND_WARNING cleared)
findings.description: set_interactive_backend.__enter__ (backend.py:1052-1065) sets the global IN_SET_CONTEXT=True BEFORE calling switch_backend(); if the switch raises (invalid name, or a real backend whose deps are missing -- e.g. TkAgg without _tkinter, exactly this audit machine), Python never calls __exit__, so IN_SET_CONTEXT stays True for the rest of the interpreter session and HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND keeps the bad value assigned in __init__ (BACKEND_WARNING was also reset to None). This is reachable through plain public calls: (a) hyp.plot(data, animate=True) after set_interactive_backend('bogus') -- manage_backend wraps the plot in this context, the switch fails, and the leak happens inside a normal plot() call; (b) `with hyp.set_interactive_backend('TkAgg'):` on a machine without Tk -- which is VERBATIM the class docstring's own example. Downstream effect (verified): every later animated/interactive plot silently SKIPS backend management entirely (manage_backend's `if not IN_SET_CONTEXT` gate), so it renders on whatever backend is current instead of an interactive one, with no warning -- and the original failure is masked (the 'bogus' backend is never re-attempted). rcParams save/restore still works (separate finally), and the matplotlib backend itself is not left switched (the switch is what failed); the corruption is hypertools' own module state.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/Users/jmanning/hypertools')
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from hypertools.plot import backend as B
data = [np.random.default_rng(1).standard_normal((30, 4))]
hyp.set_interactive_backend('bogus')          # accepted silently (see 003)
try:
    hyp.plot(data, animate=True, duration=1, frame_rate=5, show=False)
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e)
print('IN_SET_CONTEXT =', B.IN_SET_CONTEXT)   # True -- leaked forever
print('HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND =', repr(B.HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND))  # 'bogus'
fig = hyp.plot(data, animate=True, duration=1, frame_rate=5, show=False)
print('silently succeeded on current backend:', type(fig).__name__)
EOF

findings.title: Nested set_interactive_backend contexts: inner __exit__ resets IN_SET_CONTEXT to False while the outer context is still active
findings.description: IN_SET_CONTEXT is a single bool, not a counter/stack (backend.py:1053-1071). After an inner `with set_interactive_backend(...)` exits inside an outer one, IN_SET_CONTEXT is False even though the outer context is still active, so manage_backend resumes per-plot backend management inside the outer block (defeating the documented skip and, for mpl-backend contexts, re-running switch/reset cycles the outer context was supposed to own). The RENDER preference itself is restored correctly through nesting (verified: outer 'plotly' still renders plotly after inner 'matplotlib' exits) because resolve_backend reads PREFERRED_RENDER_BACKEND, not IN_SET_CONTEXT -- so for render backends the impact is limited to the redundant management; for matplotlib GUI-backend contexts it can additionally re-trigger BACKEND_WARNING emission and extra backend switches per plot.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/Users/jmanning/hypertools')
import hypertools as hyp
from hypertools.plot import backend as B
with hyp.set_interactive_backend('plotly'):
    with hyp.set_interactive_backend('matplotlib'):
        pass
    print('inside outer context, IN_SET_CONTEXT =', B.IN_SET_CONTEXT)
EOF

findings.title: The render-backend form set_interactive_backend('plotly'|'matplotlib') -- the only global way to prefer plotly -- is completely undocumented in the user-facing docstring/API docs
findings.description: set_interactive_backend's class docstring (backend.py:922-1014) describes ONLY matplotlib GUI backend keys ('TkAgg' etc.: 'Manually set the `matplotlib` backend used for generating interactive plots'); the 'plotly'/'matplotlib' render-preference routing exists only in code comments (QC 2026-07) and resolve_backend's internal docstring. docs/api.rst autodocs that same docstring, and no gallery example uses the render form (plot_interactive_backend.py / animate_plotly.py only pass backend='plotly' per call). Consequences verified in this audit: the render form works (globally, as context manager, case-insensitively, overrides Kaggle auto-detection) but a scientist reading the docs cannot discover it. Related asymmetry, same doc hole: $HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND=plotly does NOT select the plotly renderer -- it warns 'failed to set matplotlib backend to backend specified in environment (plotly). Falling back to MacOSX' -- even though plot()'s docstring presents the env var and set_interactive_backend() as equivalent overrides.

findings.title: save_path='.html' (plotly interactive export) works but is undocumented; save-format support is asymmetric across backends and the save_path docstring only describes the matplotlib/FFMPEG story
findings.description: plot()'s save_path docstring (plot.py:660-668) says 'Path to save the image/movie' + FFMPEG notes only. Verified behavior: on the plotly backend, save_path='x.html' writes a fully self-contained interactive HTML (static AND animated -- animated htmls embed all frames and play in a real browser; verified via Playwright, ~4.9 MB each); on the matplotlib backend the same call raises ValueError: "Format 'html' is not supported (supported formats: eps, jpeg, jpg, pdf, pgf, png, ps, raw, rgba, svg, svgz, tif, tiff, webp)". Neither the html capability nor the asymmetry is documented anywhere (docs example animate_plotly.py documents only .gif/.png/.mp4 'on either backend'). fig.write_html() is implicitly available since plot() returns the plotly Figure (documented), but save_path is the discoverable path. Static plotly exports to png/pdf etc. route through kaleido (see finding 011).

findings.title: No public way to reset the render preference to auto-detection once set
findings.description: After any set_interactive_backend('plotly'|'matplotlib') call, PREFERRED_RENDER_BACKEND is permanently 'plotly' or 'matplotlib' for the session; the None (auto: plotly on Colab/Kaggle, matplotlib elsewhere) state is unreachable through the public API -- set_interactive_backend(None) does not mean 'auto', it corrupts HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND to the string 'None' (finding 003). A user who wants to return to environment-based auto-detection must reach into hypertools.plot.backend.PREFERRED_RENDER_BACKEND (itself hard to import; finding 009) or restart. Suggest set_interactive_backend('auto') or (None) to restore auto-detection.

A one-time UserWarning in set_interactive_backend (or at first resolve) would make the two paths consistent.

findings.title: `import hypertools.plot.backend as B` fails with a confusing error because the plot() function shadows the plot subpackage attribute; the plot() docstring references this exact module path
findings.description: hypertools/__init__.py line 4 (`from .plot.plot import plot`) rebinds the package attribute `hypertools.plot` to the FUNCTION, so the `import a.b.c as x` binding form -- which walks attributes -- fails with "cannot import name 'backend' from 'plot' (unknown location)" (the bare 'plot' is the function's __name__; 'unknown location' because a function has no __file__). `from hypertools.plot import backend` and importlib.import_module both still work. plot()'s mpl_backend docstring points users at `hypertools.plot.backend.HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND`, and `hypertools.plot.backend.HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND` is NOT reachable by attribute access on the function either -- users must know the from-import workaround. Long-standing hypertools naming collision, but the confusing message + docstring reference make it worth a docs note or a `hypertools.backend`-style alias.
findings.expected: Module imports (or the docstring points at an importable path)
findings.actual: ImportError: cannot import name 'backend' from 'plot' (unknown location)

findings.title: plotly title-size comment '12pt = 16px' uses the CSS 96-dpi conversion the same module explicitly rejects for markers/lines (100 dpi -> 12pt = 16.67px)
findings.description: plotly_backend.py:839 comment 'match matplotlib: centered black title (12pt = 16px)' and layout title font size=16. The module's own PT_TO_PX block (lines 57-68) argues at length that the correct conversion at hypertools' shared 100-dpi canvas is 100/72 (NOT 96/72), and every line width/marker size uses it; the title alone uses the 96-dpi value (12*96/72=16 instead of 12*100/72=16.67). Sub-pixel visual impact; flagging for internal consistency of the parity math (rendered plotly titles are ~0.7px smaller than matplotlib's).
findings.expected: 16.666... px per the module's own 100-dpi rule (or a comment acknowledging the deliberate rounding)
